article.story: CORAL GABLES, Fla. -- — Shelton Henderson scored a season-high 22 points on 8-of-11 shooting and No. 17 Miami beat Manhattan 106-54 on Friday night. Nick Dorn made a career-high seven 3-pointers and finished with 21 points, while freshman Caleb Gaskins added 14 points for the Hurricanes (5-1), who had six players finish in double figures. Acaden Lewis scored 13 points, Somto Cyril had 11 points and eight rebounds and Dante Allen finished with 10 points. It was the Hurricanes’ fifth consecutive win of 35 points or more and their first 100-point performance since a 105-67 win over North Florida on Dec 21, 2025. The Hurricanes shot 38 of 70 from the field and had a 26-4 advantage on points off turnovers. They also scored 28 fast-break points. Malik Reneau, Miami’s leading scorer last season, sat out his second straight because of an upper-body injury. The Jaspers (1-5) didn’t have a player score in double figures. Ben Pearce and Quron Elliot finished with nine points apiece. After leading 53-32 at the break, the Hurricanes stretched the advantage to 68-37 on Gaskins’ fast break dunk seven minutes into the second half. Miami struggled from the field and free throw line early before a 13-2 spurt helped build its double-digit advantage. Henderson’s dunk with 7:14 remaining capped the surge and put the Hurricanes ahead 31-16. Brent Bland’s 3-pointer with 46 seconds left gave the Hurricanes their largest lead of the half at 51-30. In the opening 10 minutes, the Hurricanes made three of their first 11 free throws and, at one stretch, missed six straight from the field, allowing the Jaspers to stay close. Up next Manhattan: At NJIT on Wednesday. Miami: Faces TCU on Tuesday in Las Vegas. ------ Sign up for Top 25 poll alerts here, visit the Top 25 here and see AP’s full men’s basketball coverage here
